metadata.case_name: LEE LUNG WAH AND OTHERS v. LAU KAM SHUN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Traumatic optic nerve damage to left eye (commotio retinae; visual acuity reduced).
source: P2's left eye became blurred after the accident. Examination by Tuen Mun Hospital on 14 November 1999 recorded a finding of commotio retinae. Visual acuity was down to 6/36. Dr Ho, his own ophthalmologist, saw him on 6 September 2001 and diagnosed it as a case of traumatic optic nerve damage. The prognosis he gave was "poor". Permanent disability to the left eye and visual system as a whole was rated at 25% and 6% respectively.

injuries.description: Dislocation of the right acromio-clavicular ("AC") joint; treated with open reduction and fixation; implant later removed; residual shoulder impairment.
source: By a report of the Orthopaedics and Traumatology Department, North District Hospital, the 2nd plaintiff ("P2") suffered both head injury and dislocation of the right acromio-clavicular ("AC") joint. Nothing, however, is mentioned in the way of treatment of the former. Open reduction and fixation only, was performed on his shoulder.
With the implant also removed on 12 January 2000, he proceeded to and received physiotherapy (shoulder mobilization exercises) until August 2000.
I accept Dr Wong's findings that P2 suffers 10 % upper extremity impairment by loss of right shoulder movement and 20% upper extremity impairment by loss of right hand grip power.

injuries.description: Radial nerve damage in left forearm resulting in numbness of left thumb.
source: As for P2's thumb, it is not contested that the numbness was due to radial nerve damage (his left forearm suffered abrasion) but no adverse effect can be found on its movement.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of radial nerve at forearm level

injuries.description: Contusion injury to the anterior chest wall (P2).
source: In the same way, Dr Wong attributes P2's chest pain to contusion injury to the anterior chest wall.

injuries.description: Bilateral pneumothorax, mild right haemothorax and right middle lobe lung contusion (P5).
source: The 5th plaintiff ("P5") sustained the following injuries during the accident - bilateral pneumothorax, mild right haemothorax and right middle lobe lung contusion. He was treated conservatively with chest drain insertion and hospitalized for 10 days.

injuries.description: Healed fractures with residual deformity of left 2nd and 4th ribs (P5).
source: According to Dr Wong, fractures with residual deformity can be seen in P5's left 2nd and 4th ribs, but not anywhere near the sternum.

manifestations.description: Reduced visual acuity (visual acuity was down to 6/36); permanent disability to the left eye and visual system rated at 25% and 6% respectively.
Left eye blurred / commotio retinae recorded on 14 November 1999.
Loss of right shoulder joint movements.
Constant nervousness about return to previous occupation.
Pain and weakness in both legs particularly when climbing up stairs (P5).
Sexual impotence (P5 complained of sexual impotence).
Increased urinary frequency (up to 30 times a day) (P5).

treatments_received: Open reduction and fixation of right acromio-clavicular joint
treatments_future: Follow-up appointments at North District Hospital (P2)
Follow-up with neurologists / further scans (P5) - as per witness evidence

losses.description: Permanent disability to the left eye and visual system rated at 25% and 6% respectively; reduced visual acuity (6/36).
Loss of right shoulder joint movements and weakness of right hand grip-power (10% and 20% upper extremity impairments respectively).
Unable to return to bar-bending; reduced ability to continue prior congenial employment due to shoulder impairment.
Bilateral pneumothorax, mild right haemothorax and right middle lobe lung contusion resulting in chest pain and breathing difficulty (P5).
Healed fractures with residual deformity of left 2nd and 4th ribs causing chest wall symptoms (P5).

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life

losses.description: Complaints of serious loss of memory (P5).
